claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has poor integrity and tends to crack.
A composition change can induce ordered L12 precipitation in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Ordered L12 precipitation will enhance the alloy's integrity.
Ordered L12 precipitation will preserve the alloy's caloric response.
The induced L12 precipitates will produce precipitation hardening.
The intervention will refine the alloy's grains.
The intervention will increase compressive strength by 20% relative to the unchanged alloy.
The intervention will improve thermal conductivity by 15% relative to the unchanged alloy.
The proposed performance is expected over operating temperatures from 250 K to 350 K.
The proposed performance is expected under applied magnetic fields up to 5 T.
The proposed performance is expected under pressures up to 100 MPa.

contradictions.description: The stated predictions are a 20% strength increase and a 15% conductivity improvement, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 10% and 5%, respectively. Results between those values would contradict the quantitative predictions without triggering falsification.
The hypothesis says caloric response will not be sacrificed, while the falsification rule permits a decrease of up to 5% without falsifying it.
